g.text: RAG: Teaching Your Chatbot to Read Your Documents
Day 4 of 10 — LLMs, RAG & Agentic AI — 2-hour session
• Knows the whole internet (up to its cutoff)
By end of session: your chatbot answers questions about any PDF you give it. Live demo.
+ let the LLM write the answer.
Retrieve + Augment + Generate. That's where the name comes from.
Slide 4 — The two phases of RAG
RAG has two phases — know which runs when
takes minutes to hours, done once
takes 1-3 seconds, happens every chat turn
The embedder is the SAME in both phases — question and docs must live in the same space.
every token costs money, every query
want the paragraph that matters, not the chapter
irrelevant text in context lowers answer quality
Small enough to be precise. Big enough to carry meaning.
Three ways to slice a document
The attendance policy applies to all students enrolled. Minimum 75% presence is mandatory.
Simple, fast, works. Problem: slices mid-word.
The attendance policy applies to all students enrolled. Minimum 75% presence is mandatory.
Keeps meaning intact. Problem: chunk sizes vary wildly.
Search on small chunks for precision, return the bigger parent to the LLM. Best of both.
— missing the subject, the LLM can't tell what 'the policy' refers to.
sentence sits whole inside one chunk
Retrieved chunk contains the full sentence:
"The attendance policy applies to all students enrolled. 75% presence is mandatory."
Overlap stops sentences from being lost at a boundary. Rule of thumb: 10-20% of chunk size.
Embeddings — turn text into numbers that carry meaning
"do I need to come to class?"
• Each piece of text becomes a point in a high-dim space.
• 'come to class' and 'attendance mandatory' live close.
• That's how we FIND the right chunk.
Similar meaning = nearby in space. The question lands near the right chunks.
That's it. One formula. Powers most of search in 2026.
The whole pipeline, with real tool names
prompt sent to LLM: "answer using ONLY these chunks, cite them"
You've just read the whole RAG stack. Now we build it.
The prompt that makes RAG work
Answer the question using ONLY the context below.
If the answer is not in the context, say "I don't know."
Cite the chunk number for every fact.
This prompt turns a chatbot into a RAG system. One template.
A working RAG chatbot in 40 lines
f"[Chunk {i+1}] {h.page_content}" for i, h in enumerate(hits)
streamlit run app.py — upload any PDF — ask questions. 40 lines.
Build your own RAG chatbot (45 min)
2. Put your Groq API key in .env
5. Upload a PDF (textbook chapter, resume, college handbook — your pick)
6. Ask 5 questions. For each, check the Sources expander —
did the right chunk get retrieved?
7. Experiment: change chunk_size to 1000, then to 200.
BONUS: swap for Ollama nomic-embed-text (fully local) • add a sidebar slider for k (top-k retrieved)
When your RAG gets it wrong
The right paragraph exists in the PDF but didn't make the top-k.
Fix: better retrieval, hybrid search, RERANKING.
Top-4 chunks all say the same thing — answer is shallow.
Model ignores context and invents stuff.
Fix: stricter prompt, evaluation loop, better model.
The single biggest quality lift most RAG systems ship. We'll build it tomorrow.
Tomorrow — Day 5 (4 hours): Agents enter the chat
a funnel — fast fetch, careful pick
Teach the LLM when to call your
• Reranked PDF Q&A (upgrade of today's build)
• Agent that answers "what's the attendance rule AND today's weather?" using both tools in one query
Bring laptops charged. 4 hours, 2 projects, by evening you'll have an agent.
